Subject: FintechCo - logging & redaction follow-up / next steps

Hi Alex — great to meet earlier. Thanks for the detailed product walkthrough. Per our call, I wanted to capture the follow-ups and confirm the specific logging/redaction requirements so we can turn around a configuration & mutual action plan quickly.

Recap (from our call):
- You want to keep request/response QA for investigations but cannot retain cleartext PII (account numbers, SSNs, card data).
- Headers: you asked that sensitive headers (Authorization, Cookie, X-Session) not be persisted.
- Trace IDs: you'd prefer trace IDs to be present for observability but are open to them being hashed/pseudonymized.
- Retention: target is 30 days for raw traces; aggregated metrics can be longer.
- Data residency: all logs for US customers must remain in the US region.

Open questions for your team:
1) Do you have a list of exact field patterns to redact (regexes) or examples we should use for default masking?
2) Any corporate/legal constraints on hashed vs. removed trace IDs? If they need to be reversible for internal investigation we should note that.
3) Will you need a signed DPA / addendum referencing logging controls and retention?

Next steps from Redwood:
- Attach: redwood-logging-controls-overview.pdf (high-level config + options: disable request logging, header stripping, pattern-based redaction, trace-id hashing).
- We'd confirm if our runtime supports per-tenant retention TTL and regional pinning for logs.
- Internal follow-up with Rishi/Neha to validate config & produce a sample config you can test.

Can you send the example patterns or a short requirements doc? If easier, we can do a 30-min technical call with your SREs/legal to align.

Thanks — talk soon.

—

Marissa — thanks for the summary and the doc. A few clarifications from our side: we'd prefer that any PII is never stored in cleartext in request/response logs. Specifically:

- Fields to redact/mask: account_number, ssn, card_number, email (in some cases), and customer_internal_id. We can share a sample mapping of field names next day.
- Headers: strip Authorization, Cookie, X-Internal-Auth, and any headers that look like session tokens.
- Trace IDs: OK to include if they are one-way hashed (SHA256 or equivalent) so we can join logs on the hash but not resolve back to original IDs.
- Retention: 30 days for raw logs, 13 months for aggregated metrics.
- Residency: US only.

I'm attaching our internal logging requirements (fintechco-logging-requirements.pdf) for reference. Legal looped me in to confirm DPA needs; they'll comment if they want an addendum.

If you can provide a sample logging config we can drop into our staging and test, that'd be ideal. I've copied Legal for visibility.

Thanks,
Alex

Alex — thanks for the requirements doc and the quick turnaround. Per our internal checks: 

Technical answers (short):
- Retention & residency: we support per-tenant retention TTLs and can pin raw logs to US-only storage.
- Header controls: we can strip a configurable list of headers (Authorization, Cookie, X-Internal-Auth, etc.) at the ingress point so sensitive headers are never persisted.
- Request/response redaction: our standard pipeline supports pattern-based redaction (regex) across request bodies, response bodies, and metadata. We can apply the field list you shared as a tenant-level rule.
- Trace IDs: we support optional one-way hashing of trace IDs (SHA256) before persisting so you can correlate sessions without storing the original value.
- Disable raw request logging: we can provide an option to disable raw request/response logging per route and instead emit only aggregated telemetry.

Attached: redwood-logging-config-sample.json (sample tenant config showing header strip, redaction rules, TTL=30d, trace-hash=true).

Mutual action plan:
1) You share the exact field names/regexes for account_number, ssn, card_number, and customer_internal_id (Alex) — target: Tue 2027-06-29.
2) Redwood (Rishi) will produce a staging tenant config and deploy to a test region (non-prod US) for FintechCo to validate — ETA: 2027-06-28.
3) Neha will send the 1-page security summary for Legal (Neha) — ETA: 2027-06-25.
4) If staging verification is successful, we'll finalize the DPA addendum and retention annex (legal teams).

Would you like a quick 30-min technical handshake with Rishi next week? I'm happy to set it up.

Best,
